raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation GLM’s clamped SwiGLU activation and FP8 activation quantization currently run as separate kernels in the Triton MoE path. This materializes an intermediate BF16 tensor and introduces an additional kernel launch and global-memory round trip. For a representative BF16 input of shape [160000, 1024], fusing these operations reduced latency from 254.39 μs to 107.13 μs—a 57.9% reduction (2.37× speedup) for the activation-and-quantization portion, excluding the surrounding MoE GEMMs. ## Modifications Extend the existing CUDA SwiGLU/quantization kernel with optional BF16 intermediate rounding and configurable rows per CTA. Fuse GLM’s clamp, SwiGLU activation, and group-wise FP8 quantization, eliminating the intermediate BF16 tensor. Preserve the original BF16 rounding behavior before quantization to maintain numerical equivalence with the separate kernels. Add an opt-in Triton MoE integration via SGLANG_OPT_MOE_ACT_QUANT_FUSION=1, guarded by the validated GLM configuration. Unsupported configurations retain the existing path. Preserve existing kernel defaults and compatibility with both non-TMA and TMA expert-row layouts. Add regression tests covering bitwise FP8 output/scale equivalence, padding handling, CUDA Graph replay, and unchanged default behavior. ## Accuracy Tests
  • GPU regression tests on the updated main-based implementation: 11 passed.
    • Bitwise equivalence of FP8 outputs and quantization scales against the separate activation and quantization kernels.
    • Coverage of different row counts and rows-per-CTA settings.
    • Zero/NaN padding handling.
    • CUDA Graph replay with updated inputs.
    • Unchanged behavior for existing callers using default kernel options.
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_glm_moe_activation_quant_fusion.py

  • Earlier validation also confirmed bitwise equivalence of full MoE outputs with the fusion enabled/disabled under both TMA and non-TMA paths.

  • Model-level GSM8K validation on the pre-migration implementation:

| Configuration | Correct / Total | Accuracy | | -- | -- | -- | | Fusion disabled | 1262 / 1314| 96.04% | | Fusion enabled| 1261 / 1314 | 95.97%|

Evaluation settings: TP4, EP1, 5-shot, 8 concurrent requests, temperature 0, maximum output length 4096, and reasoning_effort=low. The difference was one question; this does not establish exact model-level equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Microbenchmark of the activation-and-quantization stage:

  • Input: BF16 tensor of shape [160000, 1024], representing approximately 17K tokens expanded by top-9 routing.
  • Quantization group size: 128.
  • SwiGLU clamp limit: 10.
  • Fused kernel: BF16 intermediate rounding enabled, 4 rows per CTA.
  • Timing method: triton.testing.do_bench.
Implementation | Latency -- | -- Separate clamp/SwiGLU and FP8 quantization kernels | 254.39 μs Fused activation and FP8 quantization kernel | 107.13 μs Improvement | 2.37× speedup / 57.89% lower latency | Implementation | Latency | | -- | -- | | Separate clamp/SwiGLU and FP8 quantization kernels| 254.39 μs | | Fused activation and FP8 quantization kernel | 107.13 μs| | Improvement | 2.37× speedup / 57.89% lower latency|

The fused path removes the intermediate BF16 tensor and combines two kernel launches into one. These measurements cover only activation and quantization, not the surrounding MoE GEMMs or the entire MoE layer.

Validation scope: The microbenchmark and GSM8K results above were collected before migration to the latest main. The updated implementation has passed the 11 GPU regression tests; performance and model-level accuracy have not yet been remeasured on the updated base.

Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. +# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Match clamp -> BF16 SwiGLU -> group FP8 quant without the intermediate."""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.activation.silu_and_mul_clamp import (
+    silu_and_mul_clamp,
+    silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.per_token_group_quant import per_token_group_quant
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA only")
+
+
+def _fused(x, *, round_to_bf16=True, rows_per_cta=4):
+    rows, width = x.shape
+    out = torch.empty((rows, width // 2), device=x.device, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.empty((rows, width // 256), device=x.device, dtype=torch.float32)
+    silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant(
+        x,
+        out,
+        scale,
+        128,
+        swiglu_limit=10,
+        round_to_bf16=round_to_bf16,
+        rows_per_cta=rows_per_cta,
+    )
+    return out, scale
+
+
+def _reference(x):
+    activated = torch.empty(
+        (x.shape[0], x.shape[1] // 2), device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype
+    )
+    silu_and_mul_clamp(x, activated, 10)
+    return per_token_group_quant(activated, group_size=128)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows", [1, 17, 1024, 4237])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows_per_cta", [1, 4])
+def test_bitwise_matches_separate_kernels(rows, rows_per_cta):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    x = (torch.randn(rows, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) * 12).contiguous()
+    expected_q, expected_s = _reference(x)
+    actual_q, actual_s = _fused(x, rows_per_cta=rows_per_cta)
+    assert torch.equal(actual_q.view(torch.uint8), expected_q.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.equal(actual_s, expected_s)
+
+
+def test_zero_and_uninitialized_padding_sanitization():
+    x = torch.zeros(17, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    x[1].fill_(float("nan"))
+    expected_q, expected_s = _reference(x)
+    actual_q, actual_s = _fused(x)
+    assert torch.equal(actual_q.view(torch.uint8), expected_q.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.equal(actual_s, expected_s)
+
+
+def test_graph_replay_uses_updated_input():
+    torch.manual_seed(7)
+    x = torch.randn(1025, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    _fused(x)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+        actual_q, actual_s = _fused(x)
+    x.normal_()
+    graph.replay()
+    expected_q, expected_s = _reference(x)
+    assert torch.equal(actual_q.view(torch.uint8), expected_q.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.equal(actual_s, expected_s)
+
+
+def test_existing_precision_default_is_unchanged():
+    torch.manual_seed(8)
+    x = torch.randn(17, 1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    actual_q, actual_s = _fused(x, round_to_bf16=False, rows_per_cta=1)
+    expected_q = torch.empty_like(actual_q)
+    expected_s = torch.empty_like(actual_s)
+    silu_and_mul_contig_post_quant(x, expected_q, expected_s, 128, swiglu_limit=10)
+    assert torch.equal(actual_q.view(torch.uint8), expected_q.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.equal(actual_s, expected_s)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, *sys.argv[1:]]))
